options.B: To make the patient feel more comfortable and relaxed
options.C: To prevent altering natural bowel sounds before listening
options.D: To ensure the procedure takes as little time as possible

explanation: Spot on! Pressing or tapping too early wakes up the tummy and makes sounds that weren't there originally. Always listen first!

question: What do we mean when we say an ultrasound is 'operator-dependent'?

options.A: The machine will not turn on unless a licensed physician is in the room
options.B: The accuracy of the results depends heavily on the skill of the person holding the probe
options.C: Patients must pay a separate fee every time the probe touches their skin
options.D: The device requires constant maintenance by an external technician

explanation: Because you have to guide the probe yourself, the picture and diagnosis depend a lot on your scanning technique and practice!

question: Which drug class is most risky for a fatal overdose because it lacks a simple reversal drug?

options.A: Z-drugs
options.B: Barbiturates
options.C: Antihistamines
options.D: Benzodiazepines

explanation: Barbiturates are very strong. Unlike benzodiazepines which have a handy reversal drug like flumazenil, barbiturates can easily cause fatal breathing arrest. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T2#GNS223_U6_T2_h2)

question: What do we call bundles of nerve fibers found entirely inside the central nervous system?

options.A: Ganglia
options.B: Tracts
options.C: Nerves
options.D: Receptors

explanation: Great to know for exams: inside the brain and spinal cord, fiber bundles are called tracts. Outside the central nervous system, we call them nerves!

question: Why are electrical toys not allowed inside or near an oxygen tent?

options.A: They interfere with the digital pulse oximeter readings
options.B: They can create small sparks that ignite the oxygen-rich air
options.C: They consume too much electricity from the hospital wall outlet
options.D: They make too much noise and frighten the pediatric patient

explanation: Oxygen feeds fire! Even a tiny spark from a toy motor can cause a serious fire hazard in an oxygen-rich space.

question: Which vaccine is super important to give if a client has a fresh, unsterilized scarification wound?

options.A: BCG tuberculosis
options.B: Tetanus toxoid
options.C: Oral polio vaccine
options.D: Yellow fever shot

explanation: Spot on! Cuts made with non-sterile tools carry a high risk of tetanus, making a booster shot a vital life-saving step.

question: What is the typical pH range of normal human semen?
explanation: Semen is mildly alkaline to survive the acidic conditions of the vaginal tract. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T3#GNS121_U4_T3_h5)

question: How do Hepatitis B and C viruses primarily cause damage inside the human body?

options.A: By blocking oxygen transport in red blood cells
options.B: By releasing toxins that paralyze skeletal muscles
options.C: By destroying CD4+ immune cells in the bloodstream
options.D: By targeting hepatocytes and triggering liver inflammation

explanation: Both Hepatitis B and C love to attack liver cells (hepatocytes), causing inflammation and gradual damage over time.

question: Why must a patient still do a biopsy after a routine screening test comes back positive?

options.A: A biopsy is necessary to cure the disease without surgery
options.B: Biopsies are required by law before any medication can be prescribed
options.C: Screening tests are always completely inaccurate for internal organs
options.D: Screening tests only suggest risk and cannot definitively diagnose cancer

explanation: Exactly! Screening tests only raise a red flag or show a risk. A biopsy (checking actual tissue cells) is the only way to say for sure that it's cancer.

question: Which of the following is a key characteristic of an effective nursing standard?

options.A: It should be written in complex legal language
options.B: It must change every single week
options.C: It should ignore available ward resources
options.D: It must be measurable and achievable

explanation: Effective standards must be realistic for staff to meet and clear enough to measure accurately. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h3)

question: Which part of the nervous system includes the sensory nerves branching out to your skin and organs?

options.A: Central nervous system
options.B: Peripheral nervous system
options.C: Autonomic sympathetic chain
options.D: Enteric digestive network

explanation: You got it! Think of the central nervous system as the main office (brain and spinal cord), while the peripheral nervous system is the field crew reaching out to every corner of the body.

question: What does client-centered care focus on the most when dealing with reproductive health?

options.A: The traditional beliefs of the senior medical doctors
options.B: The rigid scheduling needs of the hospital administration
options.C: The personal preferences and autonomy of the individual
options.D: The financial targets set by the facility management

explanation: Brilliant! Client-centered care puts the patient in the driver's seat, respecting their personal choices and rights over their own body. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T2#GNS312_U5_T2_h3)

question: Why might a patient's vomit turn a bright green or yellow color?

options.A: It is a normal sign of eating green vegetables
options.B: It indicates that food was digested properly in the small intestine
options.C: It proves the patient has a severe bacterial lung infection
options.D: It often appears after prolonged vomiting when the stomach is empty

explanation: Once the stomach is completely empty from throwing up, continuous vomiting brings up bright green or yellow bile from the small intestine.

question: What usually happens to ordinary families when they have to pay heavy out-of-pocket costs for healthcare?

options.A: Guaranteed reimbursement of medical bills by local governments
options.B: Catastrophic health expenditures that drain household savings
options.C: Automatic enrollment in free federal health insurance schemes
options.D: Immediate access to advanced surgical care in private hospitals

explanation: When you have to pay straight from your pocket without insurance, sudden illnesses can easily wipe out a family's savings and drag them into severe poverty.

question: Why can sending random, unrequested donations by the public sometimes cause trouble during a disaster?

options.A: They violate international trade laws regarding tax exemptions
options.B: They clog ports and waste time sorting items that cannot be used
options.C: They reduce the funding available for local volunteer stipends
options.D: They automatically trigger a mandatory audit by the United Nations

explanation: Spot on! Well-meaning boxes of random clothes or expired goods end up blocking logistics hubs, wasting precious time when people need actual medical supplies.

question: What is the main goal of Behavioural Change Communication (BCC) in public health?

options.A: To promote positive and healthy behaviour choices
options.B: To replace modern medicine with traditional remedies
options.C: To distribute free medical equipment to hospitals
options.D: To punish communities that ignore health guidelines

explanation: Spot on! BCC is all about working together with individuals and communities to help them build healthier lifestyle habits.

question: A patient struggles to understand a complicated medication schedule with four different drugs. What is the best initial nursing action?

options.A: Tell the patient to double the morning dose instead
options.B: Scold the patient for being careless with prescriptions
options.C: Stop all the medications until the patient feels better
options.D: Work with the doctor to simplify the dosing schedule

explanation: Simplifying complex regimens reduces confusion and makes it much easier for the patient to follow the treatment plan. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T5#GNS215_U4_T5_h7)

question: What is the main reason for assessing lung sounds before giving a nebulizer treatment?

options.A: To clear out thick mucus plugs before the machine is turned on
options.B: To establish a baseline for evaluating the treatment's effectiveness later
options.C: To find out if the patient has a hidden bacterial chest infection
options.D: To calculate the exact dose of medicine needed for the patient

explanation: Checking lung sounds beforehand helps the nurse compare wheezing or air entry after the treatment ends. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h3)

question: A nurse is teaching a mother how to support her child with cerebral palsy at home. What is the most important nursing action?

options.A: Discourage the child from participating in play activities
options.B: Encourage consistent daily exercises and proper use of prescribed braces
options.C: Advise the mother to stop all therapy sessions once the child starts school
options.D: Tell the family to avoid using any mobility assistive devices

explanation: Consistency at home with therapy routines and assistive devices is vital for maintaining physical gains. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h5)

question: Why is it smart to partner with existing groups like age-grades or church/mosque committees?

options.A: They are legally required to manage government health clinics
options.B: They provide a steady source of income for health workers
options.C: They already hold influence and command trust among members
options.D: They possess formal medical training recognized by the ministry

explanation: Spot on! Working through groups that people already belong to and trust makes it much easier to share important health messages.

question: Which of these body processes slows down when the sympathetic system takes over?

options.A: Pulmonary airflow
options.B: Sweat gland secretion
options.C: Skeletal muscle contraction
options.D: Gastrointestinal digestion

explanation: Your gut takes a back seat during emergencies. Blood goes to the muscles instead of digesting your last meal!

question: An older patient only eats tea and bread every day. What is the best next step for the nurse?

options.A: Collaborate with a dietitian to plan nutrient-dense meals and snacks
options.B: Scold the patient for having poor eating habits
options.C: Document that the patient has perfect nutritional status
options.D: Discharge the patient immediately since they are eating something

explanation: You're a natural! Once you spot a nutritional gap, teaming up with a dietitian is the best way to help the patient eat healthier.

question: What happens when someone's line of gravity moves outside their base of support?

options.A: Muscle strength instantly doubles
options.B: Blood pressure drops to zero
options.C: Joint flexibility increases
options.D: The person loses balance and falls

explanation: Spot on! If your center of balance wanders outside your footing, gravity takes over and down you go. That's why wide stances keep us steady.

question: How should nurses view technology in home health care?

options.A: As a total replacement for in-person nursing visits
options.B: As a tool to support connection and monitoring, not replace personal touch
options.C: As an unnecessary distraction that has no clinical value
options.D: As a device that only doctors are allowed to operate

explanation: Tech is a wonderful assistant for monitoring, but it can never replace the warmth and care of a human nurse sitting by the bedside.

question: When does an emergency officially become a disaster for a local community?

options.A: Any minor accident involving multiple injured people
options.B: An event that overwhelms the community's capacity to cope
options.C: An emergency that requires no external assistance
options.D: A crisis that only affects wealthy industrial areas

explanation: You've got this! A disaster simply means the local resources and helpers are stretched past their limit by the scale of the event.

question: A patient with a back injury to the vertebrae has damage in which body cavity?

options.A: Thoracic cavity
options.B: Cranial cavity
options.C: Pelvic cavity
options.D: Spinal cavity

explanation: Great thinking! The spinal cavity is enclosed by the backbone (vertebral column) and holds the delicate spinal cord.

question: What does viewing a patient in their social context primarily involve?

options.A: Isolating the patient from family members during treatment
options.B: Recognizing how relationships and living conditions affect health
options.C: Focusing strictly on the diseased organ and laboratory values
options.D: Prioritizing hospital policies over community traditions

explanation: Social context looks at the broader picture of a person's life, including family and living conditions, which deeply influence health outcomes. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h1)

question: What are haematinics?

options.A: Enzymes that break down dietary proteins
options.B: Hormones that stimulate white cell immunity
options.C: Proteins that destroy old red blood cells
options.D: Nutrients needed for blood cell formation

explanation: Think of haematinics as the body's building blocks (like iron and vitamins) used to manufacture fresh, healthy red blood cells. You've got this!

question: What is improvisation in the context of instructional materials?

options.A: Teaching without any visual or practical aids
options.B: Purchasing expensive imported anatomical models
options.C: Creating teaching aids from local, low-cost materials
options.D: Relying solely on digital online simulations

explanation: Improvisation uses available local resources to build effective teaching tools when standard commercial equipment is unavailable. [learn more](GST321_U8_T4#GST321_U8_T4_h6)

question: Why might a nurse choose group counselling over individual counselling for a diabetes education program?

options.A: It allows the nurse to give private, confidential medical diagnoses
options.B: It reaches multiple patients at once and encourages shared learning
options.C: It is the only legal method to teach carbohydrate counting
options.D: It completely prevents patients from asking questions about food

explanation: Groups are efficient for widespread conditions like diabetes, saving time while building a supportive community spirit. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T002#GNS227_U7_T002_h3)

question: What is the very first thing you should do before putting any topical medication on a patient's skin?

options.A: Massage the skin vigorously to increase blood flow
options.B: Apply a thick layer of petroleum jelly to protect surrounding tissue
options.C: Warm the cream under hot running water
options.D: Assess the condition and integrity of the target skin area

explanation: Always check the skin first! You need to make sure there are no unexpected cuts, open wounds, or signs of infection that would change your plan.

question: Parenteral nutrition delivers concentrated calories and nutrients directly into which part of the body?

options.A: The muscular tissue of the upper thigh
options.B: The bloodstream through a central venous catheter
options.C: The stomach cavity through a percutaneous tube
options.D: The small intestine through a nasal tube

explanation: Parenteral nutrition bypasses the gut completely and sends nutrients straight into the bloodstream via a central line.

question: Your patient just took a sip of water and now sounds wet and gurgling when they speak. What is your very first nursing move?

options.A: Document normal finding and continue the meal
options.B: Stop feeding immediately and assess the airway
options.C: Encourage the patient to talk more to clear the voice
options.D: Offer a thicker fluid to clear the throat

explanation: That wet voice is a red flag telling you liquid has hit the vocal cords! Stop the meal right away to protect your patient from choking or lung infections.

question: Which group of symptoms strongly points towards preeclampsia in a pregnant patient?

options.A: Low blood pressure, excessive sleepiness, and hunger
options.B: Frequent urination, mild thirst, and dry skin
options.C: High blood pressure, headache, and visual disturbances
options.D: Lower back pain and increased appetite

explanation: You nailed it! Preeclampsia is marked by high blood pressure paired with stubborn headaches and blurry vision. Always watch out for this!

question: What standard framework guides disease reporting forms in Nigerian health facilities?

options.A: Standard Operating Procedures for Pharmacy Inventory
options.B: National Curriculum for Basic Nursing Education
options.C: Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response (IDSR)
options.D: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS)

explanation: IDSR is the golden framework we use across Nigerian facilities to keep our disease tracking organized and consistent. You'll see this a lot in practice!

question: What typically happens to the risk of early marriage during wars, displacement, or natural disasters?

options.A: The risk disappears as international aid organizations provide complete financial security.
options.B: The risk increases significantly due to the breakdown of social and protection systems.
options.C: The risk remains unchanged because marriage laws are strictly enforced globally.
options.D: The risk decreases because communities focus entirely on rebuilding infrastructure.

explanation: You got it! Crises destroy normal community supports, leaving families vulnerable and sometimes driving them toward early marriage as a desperate survival measure.

question: As a working nurse, why is it helpful to understand basic data processing?

options.A: To help them evaluate new hospital guidelines and clinical research
options.B: To replace hospital statisticians during busy morning shifts
options.C: To manage the hospital financial payroll system directly
options.D: To diagnose rare diseases without using laboratory tests

explanation: You don't need to be a statistician! Knowing how data turns into evidence helps you decide if a new hospital guideline is actually trustworthy for your patients.

question: Which screening is especially important before starting a patient on a strict low-calorie diet?

options.A: Measuring adult visual acuity levels
options.B: Testing for chronic seasonal allergies
options.C: Evaluating natural hair color changes
options.D: Screening for history of eating disorders

explanation: Correct! Strict calorie tracking can trigger unhealthy eating habits, so checking a patient's history first is an important safety step.
